why_this_file_exists: T1 evidence item 3 treats a clean DRC verdict from a deck with undisclosed coverage holes as a false claim. This file is the disclosure, pinned to the exact deck revision it describes by `content_hash`. flow/check_records.py refuses to accept a DRC record whose deck content hash does not equal the value above, so this enumeration cannot silently go stale behind a deck upgrade: bumping klt forces this file to be re-derived and re-reviewed.

what_it_is: klt's own headless, pip-only rule deck built from KLayout Region check primitives. It is a deliberately partial, curated transcription of the sky130 DRM -- NOT the PDK-native sky130A.lydrc deck, and not a signoff deck. It is what `klt drc --engine curated --deck sky130` runs.

known_gaps.summary: 47 rules, not the full DRM. Whole rule chapters have no representation at all.
known_gaps.detail: The deck covers width / spacing / enclosure / separation checks over poly, diff, li1, licon1/mcon, met1-met5, via1-via4, the MiM-cap stack (capm/capm2), and nwell. There are no antenna rules, no density rules, no latch-up rules, no implant (nsdm/psdm) rules, no deep-nwell rules, no pad/seal-ring rules, and no rules on any layer outside the scope list. A `status: clean` verdict is a statement about those 47 rules only.

known_gaps.summary: m2.6 (minimum met2 area, 0.0676 um^2) is not transcribed, and no area-class rule of any kind is present for sky130.
known_gaps.detail: Authoring area / density / antenna rules for this deck is tracked upstream as candidate follow-on work rather than silently dropped. Consequence for this repo: a sliver of met2 below the minimum-area threshold would pass.

known_gaps.summary: nwell's enclosure of opposite-type diffusion/tap (difftap.8, difftap.10) is deliberately not transcribed.
known_gaps.detail: Both official rules are scoped to a psdm/nsdm implant-layer boolean expression. The deck's extraction side has no psdm/nsdm fields, so the rules are left explicitly open rather than approximated by an unscoped stand-in. See the 'nwell (well-layer) rule coverage' note in sky130.py's module docstring.

known_gaps.summary: diff.width.1 approximates the official difftap.1 rule, which is defined on the compound layer diff.or(tap), by checking diff.drawing alone.
known_gaps.detail: The Region check primitives evaluate one layer, or one layer against one other layer, at a time -- they do not evaluate arbitrary layer boolean expressions the way a DRC-DSL script runner does. A width violation that exists only on the diff-or-tap union, and not on diff alone, is not caught.

known_gaps.summary: via.width.1 / via2.width.1 / via3.width.1 / via4.width.1 enforce only the minimum-size half of their source rules.
known_gaps.detail: Each official via rule additionally requires the cut be rectangular and capped at a maximum length (e.g. via.1a_a / via.1a_b). The width_check primitive supports a minimum-width lower bound only, so an oversized or non-rectangular cut passes.

known_gaps.summary: li1.enclosing.licon1.1 is the one rule in the deck whose threshold is deliberately NOT its source value: 0.0 um instead of li.5's 0.08 um.
known_gaps.detail: li.5 requires its 0.08 um margin on only two adjacent edges of each cut -- a per-edge-pair conditional the rule vocabulary cannot express, and real standard-cell layout relies on it (a minimum-width li1 strap sits flush with the cut on the other two edges). The rule is transcribed at li.5's unconditional floor: 'li1 must actually cover the licon1 cut it lands on'. That catches a conductor missing part of its cut with no false positives on correct geometry; the 0.08 um two-adjacent-edges half stays uncovered. This gap is load-bearing for this repo: every geometry checked here is standard-cell layout, which is exactly the geometry class the exception was created for.

known_gaps.summary: The wide-metal spacing exceptions m1.3ab (0.28 um), m2.3ab (0.28 um), m3.3cd (0.4 um) and m4.5ab (0.4 um) are not modelled.
known_gaps.detail: Only each layer's general-case minimum spacing is checked. A wide metal shape that must honour the larger spacing, but honours only the general-case value, passes.

known_gaps.summary: Each via-enclosure rule models only its primary variant; the relaxed and area-scoped refinements are absent.
known_gaps.detail: Affected: met1.enclosing.mcon.1 (sibling refinement m1.5 absent), met1.enclosing.via.1 (via.5a, 0.085 um, absent), met2.enclosing.via.1 (m2.4_b periphery-scoped 0.045 um and m2.5 0.085 um both absent), and the met2/met3/met4/met5 enclosure rules for via2/via3/via4 in the same shape. The deck models no areaid.* layers anywhere, so no area-scoped variant of any rule can be expressed.

known_gaps.summary: li1.width.1 drops the source rule's not_in_cell5_li exclusion and applies the general-case threshold everywhere.
known_gaps.detail: The official li.1 rule exempts a handful of named analog macro cells. Those cells are not modelled here; the general-case 0.17 um threshold is applied unconditionally. This is conservative (it can only over-report), so it cannot hide a defect -- recorded for completeness.

known_gaps.summary: Two further coverage facts are per-run, not per-deck, and are recorded from each run's own output rather than here.
known_gaps.detail: Every klt drc JSON envelope carries a `coverage` block with `rules_skipped` (rules whose layers are absent from this particular stream, so they never executed) and `layers_in_stream_without_rules` (layers present in the stream that no rule in the deck references). Both are copied verbatim into each DRC evidence record. A clean verdict alongside a long `layers_in_stream_without_rules` means most of the drawn geometry was never examined -- read them together, never the verdict alone.

not_a_gap: The deck is run headlessly through KLayout's native Region primitives in-process -- there is no standalone klayout binary, GUI, or Qt dependency involved, and no subprocess whose exit status could be misread as a verdict.
